To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the serum proteome changes in patients with prostate cancer treated with RT were low, 2) the majority of changes in the serum proteome were detected between the pre-treatment sample and a sample collected after 3-4 weeks of RT (about 25% of the registered peptides had significantly changed abundances), 3) the intensity of observed serum proteome changes was not correlated with the degree of radiation toxicity or the irradiated tissue volumes, 4) a few proteins
partial-body irradiation during cancer RT induces a response of the irradiated tissues and that this response is reflected at the level of the serum peptidomic profile.
the response to radiation in prostate cancer patients was weaker compared to patients with head and neck cancer, although it is still detectable at the level of peptidome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for the biomarkers of radiation toxicity in patients with prostate cancer treated with IMRT.
the identification of the most informative proteins in serum, which could be used as potential biomarkers of the radiation response.
the identification of serum proteins that are involved in the response of irradiated patients to RT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
partial-body irradiation during RT of prostate cancer patients does not have a major effect on serum proteome.
the changes observed at the serum proteome level are low in this cohort of patients with prostate cancer treated by RT.
the partial-body irradiation in patients with prostate cancer treated with IMRT has little effect on the composition of serum proteome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
partial body irradiation during RT of prostate cancer has only a minor effect on the composition of serum peptidomes and proteomes, although some specific proteins are affected.
partial body irradiation in patients treated with IMRT has little impact on the composition of serum proteome, although there are some specific proteins whose levels are changed in the course of RT.
the partial body irradiation during prostate cancer radiotherapy has little effect on the composition of serum proteome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the partial-body RT in the prostate cancer patients has a low impact on serum proteome, which is in contrast to the head and neck cancer group.
the partial body irradiation during prostate cancer radiotherapy has little effect on the composition of serum proteome.
serum proteome can be used as an additional tool to monitor the response of patients to RT.
